findings.summary: The submission omits the categorized charged-SRAM caps and positive margin required by the active AP-stage VO-002 evidence plan.
findings.counterexample: A contract decomposition can proceed with only the aggregate 2048-byte ceiling while persistent state, stack, shared memory, or other simultaneously live categories have no bounded allocation. The ceiling alone does not establish a credible envelope.
findings.authority: process/ledgers/vo_ledger-AS-001-v2-active.yaml requires a credible categorized charged-SRAM envelope, attribution, and positive margin at AP stage; knowledge/architecture/AS-001/verification_plan-v3.md assigns this evidence to AP. C-002-SCOPE-001 requires allocations for every charged category with margin and explicit assumptions.
findings.required_resolution: Supply a credible nonoverlapping category budget and positive reserve with explicit assumptions, or use an independently authorized revised evidence path. The old AP-002 draft envelope does not automatically close this finding: it is conditional and assumes a specific task/IRQ topology, heap prohibition, and category ownership not adopted by v5. Keep physical layout and implementation measurements under VO-002.

findings.summary: Reset outcome is stated, but the reset operation's lifecycle precondition is not; concurrent reset and accepted-sample behavior can change the required window result.
findings.counterexample: A legal sample is accepted while reset clears the ring and accumulator. One implementation may include that sample in the new window, another may erase it, and another may leave a mixed state; all can follow the text because reset coordination and concurrency are explicitly unspecified.
findings.required_resolution: Define an interface-level reset lifecycle/ordering rule sufficient to preserve exactly one update per accepted sample across reset, or state a justified quiescent precondition. This need not select an ISR/task topology or synchronization primitive.

findings.summary: The result's mathematical range is defined, but no externally usable result operation or coherent visibility point is defined.
findings.counterexample: A consumer reads while the accumulator changes and observes an intermediate value, or has no specified operation by which to obtain the post-update result. The drafts explicitly leave visibility during update and publication unspecified, so the externally observable-value claim has no implementable interface behavior to check.
findings.required_resolution: Define an abstract result handoff, such as the value associated with a completed accepted-sample operation or a coherent result-read operation, including a representation capable of the full stated range. Leave concurrent-reader guarantees conditional on authorized integration semantics; do not invent atomic primitives or platform topology.

findings.summary: The draft adds mandatory invalid-input rejection without identifying authority for invalid-input behavior, while its reporting and recovery semantics remain unresolved.
findings.required_resolution: Either cite approved authority for rejection and define the acceptance indication needed by the caller, or keep the contract boundary limited to legal inputs and remove this additional behavior. Range checking needed to protect legal-input arithmetic remains an implementation obligation under VO-006.

findings.summary: Publisher continuity has no named integration owner or evidence, but v5 correctly states it as the upstream publisher's external, unverified responsibility and assigns no detector-side loss protocol.
findings.required_resolution: Preserve this as an explicit external assumption under the approved baseline. If a separately approved integration contract is introduced, assign its owner, criterion, and evidence stage there; no physical continuity evidence is required to accept the detector-side contract under the current scope.
